page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by 64 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 physical cores using the arm64 architecture. Operating at 2.6 GHz with a single thread per core, the processor features 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 64 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 3800 GB NVMe SSD instance store, and it supports a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core testing, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark memory scoring. Multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng and memory bandwidth tests—both cached small block and uncached large block—rank in the top 25%. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also demonstrate strong performance. Single-core benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, fall into the average tier, while LLM text generation on small models represents a performance bottleneck.

The m7gd.metal offers high resource density and qualitative cost-efficiency by combining dedicated ARM physical cores with high-speed DDR5 memory and a large local NVMe SSD. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, database hosting, Redis caching layers, and high-throughput static web serving. However, the lack of a GPU and average single-core performance represent clear tradeoffs for intensive single-threaded tasks or heavy LLM text generation.
